h1: Can you convert an existing garage into an ADU in Newton, MA?
title: Newton Garage Conversion ADUs: Existing Structures and Permit Rules
description: Review Newton's rules for converting a lawful existing garage or accessory structure into an accessory dwelling unit.
short_answer: Newton allows certain existing garages and other accessory structures to be converted into detached ADUs, subject to the City's size, zoning, and building-code requirements. A qualifying existing structure may be eligible for a larger by-right ADU under Newton's four-year condition. The conversion still needs the required building and safety approvals.

facts.text: Newton's ADU guidance identifies an existing structure, including a garage, as a possible location for a detached ADU and describes conditions for the 1,200-square-foot by-right path.
The state ADU regulation does not supersede the Massachusetts Building Code or Fire Code.

qa.q: Does an existing garage automatically qualify for a 1,200-square-foot ADU?
qa.a: No. Newton lists conditions involving the existing structure and its approval history. The property's specific situation must be checked against the current ordinance.

items: Whether the garage was lawfully established and meets Newton's four-year condition
Whether the conversion meets the ADU size and gross-floor-area limits
Whether the existing setbacks and height comply or have nonconforming status
Required foundation, insulation, vapor barrier, and fire-separation work
Utility connection and separate service requirements
Historic review if the structure may be historically significant
